results.title: [PDF] Heroics of the false: a new look at noir. - UNSWorks
results.content: Heroics of the false: a new look at noir. Downloaded from http://hdl.handle.net/1959.4/29485 in https:// unsworks.unsw.edu.au on 2026-05-10 HEROICS OF THE FALSE: A NEW LOOK AT NOIR JENNIFER S. BREUKELAAR A Creative Work and Thesis submitted in total fulfilment of the requirements of the degree of Doctor of Philosophy. To investigate these issues, I have chosen to illustrate my argument by analysing my novel, Viper, and two films that renew the noir cycle at different socio-political crossroads in America: in 1958, Alfred Hitchcock’s late noir, Vertigo, and in 1974, Frances Ford Coppola’s neo-noir, The Conversation. In proceeding thus, I argue in the dissertation that film noir’s most innovative borrowing can be described as a monstrous stitching together of incompatible parts—the real and the imaginary, the past and the present, the living and the dead—which accounts for a cut both between, and within, the image. I do this by fusing Marie Hélène Huet’s conception of the monstrous imagination, which is a theory of art, with Gilles Deleuze’s powers of the false, which belongs to a philosophy of time.
